page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a high-frequency compute-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, this instance features 40 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core configuration on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 4.8 GB per core. It utilizes the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate stable mid-range performance across compute and memory operations. The processor achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only cached small block rate of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 48.09 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec and processed 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server handled LLM prompt processing at 1841.39 tokens per second using a 135M parameter model, though performance scales down to 56.94 tokens per second for a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge offers dedicated compute resources without the overhead of bundled local storage or GPU hardware, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads that require predictable execution times. The absence of local storage requires external block storage integration, which represents a structural tradeoff in I/O-intensive scenarios. This instance is suitable for multi-threaded decompression tasks, software compilation, database operations, and web serving applications that benefit from high-frequency dedicated Intel Xeon cores and a balanced memory allocation.
